free_tier.stated: R500 of welcome credit after the first card payment, once per card; credits never expire. Free accounts can run 2 sandboxes at a time, each with up to 2 vCPU, 2 GB of memory and 5 GB of disk.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a sandbox with up to 5 GB of disk on a free account, not a stored object

retention.stated: Files, installed packages and browser logins live on persistent disks and survive restarts; when credits run out, running sandboxes are paused rather than deleted.

egress.terms: Sandboxes cannot reach each other, private networks or cloud metadata; egress is limited to the public internet. Managed internet transfer is not separately priced on the pricing page.

interface_detail: A public HTTPS address per sandbox, SSH access, file APIs, a Python SDK and a hosted MCP server at api.ventaw.com/mcp.
tooling: Python SDK, REST API, hosted MCP server, SSH and file APIs; noVNC for browser and desktop templates.
chaining: R0.45 per vCPU-hour and R0.15 per GB-hour put a two-vCPU, 4 GB sandbox near R1.50 an hour; a public HTTPS URL lets an agent hand results to a separate object-storage record.

binding_note: The R500 welcome credit is spendable only after a first card payment and bounds how long a sandbox runs; the two-sandbox cap bounds concurrency, not the balance.

identity_cost.detail: Sign-up asks for first name, surname, email and password, or a third-party sign-in; usage is charged in rand from a prepaid balance topped up by card through Paystack, and the R500 credit is released only after the first card payment.

reliability_note: When the prepaid balance reaches zero, running sandboxes are paused; the vendor states it does not promise that the service will never be interrupted and does not promise data restoration from backups.
confidence_note: Prices, the welcome credit, the free-account caps and the signup fields are quoted from the vendor's own pricing page, terms and sign-up page read on 2026-11-25.
